## Description
 With calcined ceramic from the previous step, the remaining process &#10;&#9;&#9;is a powder metallurgy route : &#10;&#9;&#9;1. Secondary milling&#10;&#9;&#9;2. Pressing (forming)&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Wet pressing (slurry + external B-field of 7–15 kOe) → anisotropic magnet (strong, directional). &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Dry pressing (no field) → isotropic magnet (weaker, magnetizable in any direction). &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Typical compaction: 0.3–0.6 kg/cm²&#10;&#9;&#9;3. Sintering&#10;&#9;&#9;4. Machining (optional)&#10;&#9;&#9;5. Magnetization&#10;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9; Mars-specific notes :&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Sintering requires a kiln at ~1,200 °C — feasible with electric resistance heating &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  (Mars has solar + nuclear power options).&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Magnetizer is the chicken-and-egg problem: you need a strong electromagnet to &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  magnetize the first ferrite magnet. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Solution: a superconducting coil (if you can produce one) or a capacitor bank, &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  plus air-core coil powered by the settlement&#39;s electrical grid. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  Even a modest 1 T pulse is enough.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Diamond machining requires diamond tooling, which must either be imported or &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  synthesized from Martian carbon (diamond anvil press from CO₂-derived carbon &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  is theoretically possible but not trivial). Alternatively, design the green &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  body to be the final shape and skip machining.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;  &#10;&#9;&#9;The mass of the finished magnet equals the mass of the sintered ferrite ceramic — &#10;&#9;&#9;there is no mass loss during pressing, sintering, or magnetization (only volume &#10;&#9;&#9;shrinkage of 10–20 % from porosity reduction).&#10;&#9;&#9;
